# CortIQ — Full Product Documentation

## What is CortIQ?

CortIQ is a web analytics platform built for the Agentic Web — the emerging era where AI agents and crawlers make up a fast-growing share of web traffic. By Q4 2025 there was one AI bot visit for every 31 human visits, up from one in 200 in Q1 2025 (TollBit, State of the Bots, Q4 2025).

CortIQ is an open-source, EU-built analytics platform with a dedicated module for classifying and analyzing AI traffic. Beyond AI intelligence it provides consent-gated visitor analytics (Cookieless or Full mode), click and scroll heatmaps, a cookieless per-link click counter, form analytics, geolocation maps, a paid-conversion attribution loop, an MCP server, and a built-in consent management platform (CMP).

**Production URL:** https://cortiq.se
**Company:** Expandtalk Corporation AB, Göteborg, Sweden
**License:** AGPL-3.0 (open source, self-hostable)
**Status:** Beta — free, open signup at https://cortiq.se/auth

---

## Core Features

### AI Bot Intelligence (the differentiator)

CortIQ classifies every AI visit into three categories — this is the core differentiator. The canonical bot registry is shared by the JS tag and the server-side ingest path:

- **Training crawlers** (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, Meta-ExternalAgent, CCBot, Bytespider) — infrastructure cost, no referral value
- **Agentic** (agent fetches via ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, Perplexity-User, plus JS-signal heuristics for in-browser AI agents) — real users acting through an AI; track and convert them. AI browsers such as Perplexity Comet or Claude for Chrome send a stock Chrome user agent and are not identified by name.
- **Citation crawlers** (PerplexityBot, OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, YouBot, DuckAssistBot) — AI search indexing, your visibility signal

Detection combines user-agent parsing with browser-type classification (visual / headless / text-based). Server-side agent measurement on the site's own server or edge counts the training and citation crawlers that never execute JavaScript. Agentic-browser journeys are reconstructed page-by-page with conversion attribution.

### Server-Side Agent Measurement (no device access)

The primary method for AI crawlers and agents. It runs on the site's own server or edge — Next.js/Vercel middleware, Netlify Edge, Cloudflare Worker, Node/Express, the WordPress plugin, or any server through an HTTP API:

- Crawler classification (training / agentic / citation) from the request user agent
- robots.txt and llms.txt fetches
- Hits on a hidden honeypot link in the server-rendered HTML
- Only bot-like requests are sent; ordinary human requests never leave the customer's server
- The IP is truncated to /24 (IPv6 /48) on the customer's server before sending; CortIQ clears the truncated IP after 30 days

It reads only the HTTP request the server already receives and does not access the visitor's device, so in our assessment it is not covered by ePrivacy Art. 5(3) (an interpretation, not settled law) (Swedish LEK 9 kap. 28 §) and needs no consent banner. The request data is still personal data under GDPR: the site operator needs a legal basis (typically legitimate interest, Art. 6.1.f) and should mention it in their privacy policy. The site operator makes the final legal assessment.

### In-Browser Bot Checks (after consent)

The tracking script's bot probe, invisible honeypot link, canary pixel/link traps and click-fraud scoring read device properties, which is device access under ePrivacy Art. 5.3. They start only after analytics consent, together with visitor analytics.

### Consent-Gated Visitor Analytics

All visitor analytics — page views, sessions, AI referrals, clicks, link click counts, scroll, heatmaps, forms, e-commerce, conversions — start only after the visitor grants analytics consent, in both modes. Legal basis: consent (GDPR Art. 6.1.a / ePrivacy Art. 5.3). Consent is valid 12 months (stored with an expiry), then re-asked.

- **Cookieless mode** — no cookies, no fingerprint, no cross-visit profile, no persistent IDs. Still requires consent.
- **Full mode** — persistent visitor ID and returning-visitor analysis after consent.
- IP anonymisation at ingest
- Optional hybrid mode with server-side GA4 for teams that want familiar reporting

### Human Visitor Analytics

- Page views, sessions, bounce rate, traffic sources
- Click heatmaps with device segmentation (desktop / tablet / mobile), rendered as canvas overlays
- Scroll-depth funnels (25 / 50 / 75 / 100% milestones)
- Cookieless per-link click counter — aggregate counts per link and button, per page and device type, no visitor ID
- Form analytics — field-level funnel and drop-off

### Conversion & Attribution

Closes the GA4 ↔ Google Ads ↔ CRM attribution gap:

- First-party click-ID capture (gclid, fbclid, msclkid, ttclid, li_fat_id) — consent-gated
- Conversion-goal health monitor (flags goals that fire too often, went silent, or split Smart Bidding signal)
- Form auto-discovery: HubSpot form GUIDs (hs_context, data-form-id), Gravity Forms and Contact Form 7
- In development: a HubSpot lead-quality → Google Ads Enhanced Conversions feedback loop and an attribution-gap dashboard

### Optimisation

- Conversion funnels, customizable KPI dashboards, segments and behavioral alerts

### Integrations

Configured in-app under Settings → Integrations — no code changes on the customer site:

- **Google Search Console** — search visibility (impressions, clicks, position, queries) plus an AI-search performance view
- **Google Analytics 4** — read-only import of traffic sources, segments, KPIs and AI-assistant referrals
- **Google Tag Manager & Consent Mode v2** — load the script via a GTM Custom HTML tag; it reads Google Consent Mode v2 set by your CMP
- **WordPress plugin** — script, consent banner and Google Consent Mode v2 for GA4
- **Cloudflare Worker** — server-side AI crawler classification
- **In development:** Google Ads Enhanced Conversions, HubSpot lead-quality loop, Meta Conversions API and GA4 Measurement Protocol (server-side conversion signals)

### GDPR & Consent (built-in CMP)

The consent banner is required for visitor analytics in both modes:

- Cookie consent management (consent banner, Google Consent Mode v2, 12-month consent expiry)
- Consent valid 12 months, then re-asked; closing the banner saves "necessary only"
- Marketing click IDs captured only with marketing consent
- Consent verified server-side (not just a client flag); authoritative server-side consent ledger for Art. 7(1) proof
- Consent-check API (consent-check): your server asks whether a session has the required consent before forwarding an event; every decision is logged
- Google Consent Mode v2; reads Cookiebot consent directly; the CortIQ banner steps aside when Cookiebot, OneTrust or a TCF v2 CMP is present
- Configurable data retention with an automated retention job; data-subject-request path

### AI & Agent-Ready

- **AI Assistant** — ask questions in natural language; answers are grounded in the customer's real data via tool-use, never hallucinated. Every insight shows the tables queried, row counts, model, tokens and duration.
- **MCP Server** — external AI agents can query analytics with a site-scoped, rate-limited API key (22 read-only tools). Reads are tenant-scoped and never bypass ownership.
- **llms.txt / llms-full.txt** published so AI systems can understand the product.

### Advanced Features

- **Visitor countries** — Leaflet.js world map and table of sessions per country, estimated from the browser time zone (no IP lookup)
- **User LTV & cohort analysis** — lifetime value with cohort grouping by first-visit month
- **Tag manager** — event, pixel, script and HTML tags without code deployment
- **WordPress plugin** (v5.4.0, same version as the tracking script) — download the zip from the dashboard; choose Cookieless or Full tracking mode

---

## Security & Privacy Posture

Built by an EU company for EU-grade compliance, security-first by design:

- **Row-Level Security on every table** — company/tenant isolation enforced at the database layer, never only in the application
- **Consent-gated behavioral data** in every mode — all visitor analytics, including page views and in-browser bot checks, require analytics consent; AI crawlers are measured server-side
- **Data minimisation** — IP anonymisation at ingest; emails SHA-256 hashed before any third-party upload
- **EU data residency** — Supabase, AWS eu-north-1; any US transfer (AI/ads) is optional, consent-gated and disclosed
- **The Agentic Layer only ever reads** through governed, tenant-scoped interfaces — AI never sees another tenant's data
- Vulnerability reports: see the responsible-disclosure policy in the repository (SECURITY.md)

---

## Technical Architecture

CortIQ is built as three clearly separated layers — a Data Layer with no AI dependency, an Agentic Layer that only reads through governed interfaces, and a cross-cutting Privacy/Compliance layer. You can self-host Data + Privacy with zero AI dependency and switch the Agentic Layer on only when you want it.

### Frontend
- React 18, TypeScript, Vite
- shadcn/ui (Radix UI), Tailwind CSS
- Recharts and Leaflet.js for visualization

### Backend
- Supabase (PostgreSQL + Deno Edge Functions)
- Row-Level Security (RLS) for multi-tenant data isolation

### Tracking Script

Installed on customer websites via a single `<script>` tag:

```html
<script src="https://cortiq.se/spa-tracking.js" data-site-id="YOUR_SITE_ID" defer></script>
```

The script handles page views, click and scroll heatmaps, session events, AI-agent detection, UTM capture and consent integration (CortIQ banner, Cookiebot). Everything the script does, including AI-agent detection in the browser, waits for analytics consent.

### API

REST API documented at https://cortiq.se/api/. Plus an MCP server so AI agents can query analytics programmatically with a site-scoped API key.

---

## What CortIQ Does NOT Include

- Spatial mouse-movement / attention overlay maps (click maps + scroll-depth funnels are supported)
- A/B or multivariate testing on your live site (no variant-assignment script)
- Data-warehouse export
- Mobile app analytics

---

## Target Users

- European SMEs with GDPR compliance requirements
- WordPress publishers
- Digital agencies managing analytics for multiple clients
- Organizations with significant or growing AI-agent traffic

---

## Competitive Position

CortIQ treats AI-traffic classification as a first-class feature. Traditional platforms (Google Analytics, Plausible, Fathom, Matomo) generally treat AI agents as bot noise and filter them out. CortIQ treats them as distinct categories — training, agentic and citation — each with its own funnel, attribution and behavior analysis. It combines AI-traffic intelligence, consent-gated cookieless analytics, a paid-conversion attribution loop and a built-in CMP in one EU-hosted platform.
